entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Fulgentius of Cartagena, born in Cartagena in the 6th century and died in 630, was a Bishop of Ecija (Astigi) in Hispania. He played a crucial role in the early Christianization of the Visigothic Kingdom, working closely with King Recceswinth to promote the spread of Christianity throughout the region. Fulgentius' efforts led to the translation of numerous Latin texts into Visigothic, which helped to establish a common literary canon for the kingdom. His work on theology and doctrine also influenced the development of Visigothic jurisprudence. Through his relationships with other prominent church leaders, Fulgentius helped to shape the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of the region. In 630, Fulgentius died, leaving behind a legacy that continued to influence the region for centuries to come. His translation of the Bible into Visigothic remains an important archaeological find, providing valuable insights into the linguistic and cultural practices of the Visigoths.
